statement: The source equates normality in E of a partial section s(Γ_i) with centralizing the finite kernel H. Normality implies centralization, but centralization only gives normality in p⁻¹(Γ_i). For normality in all E one additionally needs E-conjugation compatibility: e s(γ)e⁻¹=s(p(e)γp(e)⁻¹).

computation.counterexample: D8 finite witness and a geometric witness satisfying the surrounding hypotheses: X=P¹_Qbar minus S, S={−1,−1/2,−1/4,1/2,2/3,4/5,2,3,5}, X′=X, Aut_Qbar(X)=C3, all automorphisms rational. Hence E=C3×G_Q. Γ_i=G_Q(√−3); its quotient Gal(Q(√−3,∛2)/Q(√−3))=C3 defines c. Graph s=(c,id) centralizes H=C3 but conjugation by complex conjugation changes c to c⁻¹, so its image is not normal. The504 Möbius candidates are exhaustively checked over exact fractions; no scan emendation is assumed. Scope qualification: this geometric witness is finitely presented over Qbar and descends to Q. It does not satisfy a literal finite-presentation-over-Q hypothesis on a scheme whose constants contain the infinite extension Qbar. The k versus ks reading at scan10 line355 is a separate unresolved alarm (claim007). The abstract finite-kernel equivalence is refuted without changing that text; the geometric witness tests the coherent geometric-base interpretation.

This asserts finite étale descent of the discrete automorphism group, not automatic representability/reducedness of an arbitrary full automorphism functor.

Changing the triple uses rational fractional-linear formulas in those coordinates, so K is unchanged. This is the minimum field over which all labelled points can be rational after such normalization; all setwise Möbius automorphisms are then defined overK. It is not generally the unlabelled field of moduli.

statement: For z↦zⁿ in characteristic zero, the nonzero special fibres are μ_n, nth roots of−j and−jbar, and nth roots of−1,1/2,2. statement: Let K be a number field and let ξ_1,...,ξ_r in K* be multiplicatively independent modulo roots of unity. The compatible radical action of G_K has finite index in Zhat^r⋊χ(G_K), hence in the full scalar affine ambient group. For a torus or a finite Galois-stable set, first pass to its finite splitting field and use independent coordinates; the finite permutation or character-module action must be retained on descent. Each ℓ-adic image has Lie dimension r+1. Over Q, in the intrinsic saturated radical automorphism group, the exact index is 2^r; this exact number is not asserted for arbitrary K or arbitrary unsaturated coordinates.

computation.method: At level n the affine image has order [K(ζ_n,G^(1/n)):K]. Its index in (Z/n)^r⋊(Z/n)* is n^r φ(n) divided by that degree, at most C[K:Q] by the opened theorem and the cyclotomic intersection bound. The closed inverse-limit image therefore has finite index, since all its finite quotient indices have this uniform bound. The ℓ-adic dimension follows from openness. C04 illustrates only the separate rational rank-one exact-index specialization.
computation.limit: This computation illustrates rank1 only; the general-rank theorem is not claimed proved by samples.

fate: Perucca–Sgobba2019 Theorem 1.1 (published p.1617) gives a uniform integer bound C(K,G) for n^r divided by [K(ζ_n,G^(1/n)):K(ζ_n)], for any number field and finitely generated torsion-free subgroup G of positive rank r. Its publisher-provided preview was opened and the exact theorem statement read, though the full proof was not opened. The finite-level affine index is at most C[K:Q], and a closed profinite subgroup with uniformly bounded finite-quotient indices has finite index; this implication is independently proved here. Passage to a splitting field gives the torus interpretation with independent coordinates. MoreeStevenhagen2014 Theorem 2.5 additionally gives the exact intrinsic rational index 2^r. PerissinottoPerucca2023 supplies explicit degree procedures, not the same universal exact index. Earlier literature is acknowledged through the opened backward references; first historical settlement is not claimed.
fate_date: General-bound paper received 9 July 2018, published online 20 May 2019; first public preprint date not established. Rational exact-index preprint 20 March 2012, publication 2014. The draft leaves themselves are not securely dated.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: The finite-index assertion for independent algebraic generators over a number field is established. The exact 2^r formula has the explicitly rational saturated scope. The manuscript’s dimension glyph and intended torus coordinate conventions remain textual questions.

statement: Kummer theory canonically gives H¹(G_Q,μ_n)≅Q*/Q*ⁿ, with cyclotomic action on μ_n, and 0→μ_n/μ_n(Q)→Z¹→H¹→0. A choice of root changes a cocycle by a coboundary. Neither an untwisted coefficient identification nor the written direct-sum formulas are generally correct.

At the inverse limit, pointwise torsion-freeness of Zhat(1) makes Z¹ torsion-free; [−1] remains nonzero of order2 in the Kummer completion. Compatible finite roots and the finite invariant Mittag–Leffler condition justify H¹=limH¹. The non-split conclusion is independently proved, not inferred from finite samples.
